known_unknown_assumption_limitation.entry: TLC Jan 2025 Parquet contains trips with pickup dates outside January (Dec 31 2024 and Feb 1 2025 observed in manifest). This is a documented TLC batching pattern, not a download error. Trips are flagged 'out_of_month', counted (22 rows), and excluded from January metrics. They are not silently dropped — their count is visible here.
'passenger_count' is nullable per TLC data dictionary — vendors are not required to record it. Null passenger_count is not treated as a validation error; it is counted in the profile null_count only.

LocationIDs 264 (Unknown) and 265 (N/A) appear in trip data but have no entry in the Socrata zone lookup. Flagged separately as 'location_unknown' (28357 rows) so their volume is visible independently from out-of-range IDs ('location_invalid').

Maximum trip duration cutoff of 360 minutes (6 hours) is an FDE judgement call — no formal TLC threshold is published. Rationale: NYC's geographic bounds (longest metered route < 35 miles) make any genuine taxi trip under 6 hours. Trips exceeding this almost certainly represent drivers who forgot to close the meter (a known TLC data quality pattern).

Maximum trip distance cap of 100 miles is an FDE judgement call, not a TLC-published threshold. Rationale: the TLC standard metered service covers NYC metro; the furthest standard airport (JFK ~17 mi, Newark ~15 mi) and even Montauk (~120 mi, special negotiated rate) fall well below this. 100 miles captures all plausible metered trips while flagging odometer errors.

Maximum fare_amount cap of $500 is an FDE judgement call. Rationale: TLC metered rate is ~$3.50/mile; at the 100-mile distance cap that yields ~$350 metered fare; adding ~$50 in tolls/surcharges gives ~$400. $500 provides headroom for edge cases while catching clearly impossible values. No TLC maximum published.

Fare-per-mile outlier bounds ($1.50/mile lower, $50/mile upper) are FDE-set based on TLC rate card analysis, not derived from a formal statistical model of the full dataset. Lower bound: below TLC minimum metered rate suggests metering malfunction. Upper bound: above $50/mile is outside the plausible range even for very short, congested trips. May need calibration with multi-month data.

Whether negative 'fare_amount' records represent disputed fares, refunds, or data corruption at the vendor level. The TLC data dictionary does not document negative values. All negative fare_amount values are flagged 'fare_invalid' and excluded from metrics.

Whether TLC applies post-publication corrections to historical Parquet files. If they do, a re-download of the same month could produce a different row count or checksum. The manifest records the download timestamp and SHA-256 to make any such discrepancy detectable.
No GPS coordinates are available in the public TLC dataset (removed since 2016). All spatial analysis is limited to zone-ID granularity (263 zones). Sub-zone patterns are not observable.

'tip_amount' captures credit card tips only — cash tips are not recorded by vendors. Fare-per-mile consistency analysis uses 'fare_amount' (metered fare) rather than 'total_amount' to avoid this asymmetry distorting the metric.
